title: Introducing SQD: Does Finishing Quality Matter?
text:
xG is only half the battle.
In soccer, we have two metrics to judge a shot’s potential: xG (the one we all know) and post-shot xG (the one we don’t). To put it simply:

Expected Goals (xG) measures a shot’s probability of scoring based on the various factors leading up to the shot. 
Post-Shot Expected Goals (PSxG) measures a shot’s probability of scoring given the position of the shot in the goalmouth. 

xG = how good was the setup?PSxG = how good was the finish?xG is a headline statistic used to measure the both the attacking quality and the defensive quality of teams. You can find xG on most league tables on major statistics sites.
On the other hand, PSxG is a backpage afterthought. It has been proven useful to identify well-performing goalkeepers, but that relegates it to the backpage of FBREF.
We can do better than this.


Research Question: Can We Use xG and PSxG to isolate attacking tendencies?
Let’s grab some data. We’re grabbing every shot from every game over the last three full seasons as well as the in-progress 2023/24 season from FBREF. 💯 🙌 🔥 to Jase Zivkovic and Tony El-Habr for their updates on the worldfootballR package. They’ve condensed literal days-long data scraping process into about 30 seconds of compiling. Fantastic work, fellas!

library(tidyverse)
library(worldfootballR)

### Every shot from every match of the top 5 European leagues
shots_top5 <- load_fb_match_shooting(
  country = c('ENG','GER','ESP','ITA','FRA'),
  gender = 'M',
  tier = '1st',
  season_end_year = 2021:2024
)

section: New Year, New Me More Sustainable Goals
text:
New Year, New Me More Sustainable Goals
January is a natural goal-setting month. Like most people, I initially rushed to improve what I saw were the worst parts of myself.
Then I reread that last sentence. Then I was sad.
I once thought that the quickest way to self-improvement comes was a counterweight of self-loathing urgency. I don’t think it’s terribly uncommon. For me, it tends to sound like:

“[Insert Unattainable Habit to Adopt] needs to happen IMMEDIATELY because everything is so awful!!!!!”

It works, but it is also absolutely exhausting: I’ve seen plenty of front-end improvement only to burn out easily and often.
Through this experience, I am beginning to learn that slow progress is lasting progress. More specifically, progress for me will require patiently re-framing my scarcity mindset, including:

accepting how far I’ve come (I’m not starting from scratch. Everything is not awful.)
celebrating my growth and learning from my mistakes (In fact, everything is pretty good! I’ve accomplished a ton, including many mistakes.)
trusting myself to stay present and keep executing, leave the future for the future. (The opportunities I’m chasing will present themselves often. I trust myself to be as present as possible when they arrive.).

Sneaky re-frame: Mistakes are progress!So this year, I’m not throwing out the old me. I’m staying present with the current version of myself, and building toward the following milestones:

Rebuild Back to Full Strength, Physically and Financially
My knee injury from lifting was just judged not to need an MRI (yay!). More great news is that I’ve kept off the 20 pounds I lost last year during the recovery process. Looking for more, but staying patient and staying strong.

Financially I’m riding through some turbulence thanks to some early-year emergencies, but we’re getting back on track after an eventful 2023.
Keep Building Upon Healthier Habits, and Fail Often
Namely, I’m keeping my spaces clean and relatively uncluttered. We’re starting there and building out. I’m also developing the habit of writing every day, which leads to…
Get That Portfolio Up!
That’s the point of this website. I’ve been sitting on serious soccer analysis for years, but I’ve struggled to keep the ideas in my head because life is busy. Dedicating more time to documenting my process will be important and helpful. We’ll see how it goes!

Planning Golf Trips
 I’d love to get back to the American Soccer Golf Tour this year. Current candidates are as follows, suggestions welcome:Find me on social media and feel free to DM course suggestions!

Raleigh, NC - Tobacco Road is a must and I have to see if the NC Courage are a bigger draw than NCFC.
Louisville, KY - Renting hickory clubs and traveling back in time, then heading to a Lou City or Racing Louisville match. By the way, Racing Louisville’s houndstooth kit is absolute 🔥🔥🔥.
Atlanta, GA - The soccer nerd vibes at a packed ATL United Game have been on the list since I saw the Footie Mob for the first time. Course suggestions are welcome.


Current Mood: 😖▶️🙃
Annoyed, but confident. I’ve been dealing with some early-year emergencies lately (nothing I’ll get into here). However, I’m pretty proud of my response so far. Upon reflection, I want to be able to handle my stress while being able to function clearly. And if I can’t, I want to be able to confront what or who is bothering me head-on, while remaining composed and affable.
Trying to be patient as possible: the problems remain stubborn and will likely stay problems for the next few months.
There will always be problems. I can control what I can control, and I can control my response to the things I can’t control.
